nodes.content: IR models trained on one dataset perform poorly when applied elsewhere, but this is invisible when only in-domain evaluation is done
Retrieval underpins open-domain QA, fact-checking, duplicate detection; robust, generalizable retrieval is practically essential
BM25, DPR, ColBERT, cross-encoders each show strong in-domain results; no systematic cross-domain comparison exists
No heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark; MultiReQA and KILT are narrow in task/domain scope
How well do diverse retrieval architectures generalize to unseen tasks and domains in a zero-shot setup?
Build BEIR: a 18-dataset, 9-task benchmark; evaluate 10 retrieval systems; quantify efficiency trade-offs; assess annotation bias

Curate diverse public datasets by task diversity, domain diversity, difficulty, annotation variety; unify format and metric (nDCG@10); evaluate pre-trained systems without fine-tuning on target domains
10 models × 18 datasets; nDCG@10; pairwise Jaccard diversity analysis; efficiency benchmarking on 1M document sample; Hole@10 bias study with 980 manual annotations
BM25 strong baseline; dense models cluster below BM25; reranking/late-interaction above; docT5query competitive

In-domain rank order inverts in zero-shot: BM25 (weak in-domain) becomes a competitive baseline; BM25+CE best overall (+11% avg); dense DPR worst (-47.7%); annotation bias inflates lexical model advantage
Cross-attention (or cross-attention-like MaxSim) is key for OOD generalization; dense models overfit to in-domain statistics; document expansion helps lexical coverage
BEIR benchmark + open-source pip package; first systematic zero-shot IR evaluation; annotation bias quantification and mitigation procedure
English only; lexical annotation bias present across many datasets; 512-token truncation; no multi-factor signals; task-specific models excluded
Community should evaluate on BEIR before claiming generalization; annotation methodology for future datasets should use diverse retrieval pooling
Multilingual tasks; long-document retrieval; multi-field and multi-factor retrieval; better annotation strategies
